claims.text: Lattice-mismatched substrates impose epitaxial strain on non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi thin films.
Epitaxial strain tunes magnetostructural coupling in non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys.
Strain-tuned magnetostructural coupling produces a smoother and less hysteretic magnetocaloric transition under low applied fields.
Arc-melted ingots or melt-spun ribbons of the alloy exhibit a single-phase hexagonal structure.
The single-phase hexagonal alloy undergoes a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition with pronounced hysteresis.
PLD on MgO or SrTiO3 can provide a calibrated lattice mismatch of approximately ±2–3% for the proposed FeMnNiGeSi films.
Suitable deposition and cooling conditions can preserve epitaxial strain while suppressing secondary phases.
Substrate-induced strain modifies atomic spacing and local crystal symmetry.
Changes in atomic spacing and local symmetry alter magnetic exchange interactions and magnetic-domain structure.
Built-in strain perturbs magnetoelastic coupling by altering the structural-transition energy landscape.
The strain-induced modulation lowers energy barriers for domain reorientation.
Lower domain-reorientation barriers broaden the first-order transition and reduce hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Strained films will have a more gradual magnetocaloric response and lower hysteretic losses than the unstrained baseline.
Strain will cause a slight shift in transition temperature.
Films on lattice-matched substrates will retain a sharper and more hysteretic transition than films with ±2–3% mismatch.
The predicted strain effects hold within the single-phase hexagonal regime for lattice mismatches up to approximately ±3%.
Strains beyond approximately ±3% may produce secondary phases or structural instabilities that confound the magnetocaloric response.

contradictions.description: The comparator is defined inconsistently: the predicted outcome refers to an unstrained baseline, the baseline field identifies bulk ingots or ribbons, and the falsification experiment uses a minimally mismatched thin film. Bulk-versus-film and strained-versus-unstrained comparisons are not equivalent.

The material_initial_state labels arc-melted ingots and melt-spun ribbons as 'as-deposited,' whereas the intervention concerns PLD-deposited epitaxial films. This creates ambiguity about the actual initial state and whether the intervention modifies an existing specimen or creates a different material form.
